topics.topic: Ownership and communication of the requirement to inspect a damaged mark before writing a new placement
questions: Which module owns the operation-level requirement to inspect a possibly damaged mark even when no placement exists, before any stored image or placement is written, and how is that requirement made known to that module?

Which module owns and knows the requirement that a damaged mark record without a placement must be checked before a new placement writes its image or record: photo_delivery orchestration, an atomic delivery_store operation, or both through an explicit contract?

quotes:
`capability:delivery_store.read_placement` and `capability:delivery_store.read_mark` read both records, so a
   damaged record stops the delivery. With an existing placement the flow answers `replayed`, with the `photo_id` of
   its mark if there is one.
judgement.why: The later delivery flow explicitly makes photo_delivery call both delivery_store readers before proceeding, so a damaged mark stops a new placement.

topics.topic: Read behavior when state-record parent folders are missing, including whether reads create them
questions: Does a read operation such as scan or an absent-record lookup create missing `PLACEMENTS_FOLDER`, `MARKS_FOLDER`, and project folders, or are those folders created only when a file is about to be written?
If the record cannot be opened because one of its newly introduced parent folders does not yet exist, is the record absent or is the operation refused as state_unavailable?

quotes: M04, or nothing when its record does not exist.

judgement.why: The later read-operation contracts return no record when it does not exist and declare both lookups read-only, so missing ancestors do not cause folder creation or state_unavailable.

topics.topic: Classification and ownership of placement-record write failures
questions: Does `delivery_store` classify a failed placement-record write as `PlacementFailure.UNREADABLE_FILE`, or does it report a storage failure that `photo_delivery`, the stated owner of the rest of A3 rule 5, must classify?

quotes: A failed write raises the operating system error, which `module:photo_delivery` turns into the failure of that photo.
judgement.why: The later write_placement contract assigns reporting of the storage error to delivery_store and its conversion into a per-photo failure to photo_delivery.

topics.topic: Containment procedure when stored-image path folders do not yet exist
questions: How is rule 1 containment established when one or more folders in the stored-image path do not yet exist: resolve the existing prefix and append checked segments, permit non-strict resolution, or fail the delivery?

quotes: Writes the stored image atomically with the mode of `STORED_IMAGE_MODE`, creating the missing folders below the binary store with `STORE_FOLDER_MODE`; each folder it creates and the image's own folder are synchronised before it returns, and a failure there is a failed write (A6 rules 2 and 3). A missing binary store is a failed write.
judgement.why: The later store_image contract says missing folders below an existing binary store are created, ruling out refusal merely because the complete destination path does not yet exist.

topics.topic: Handling folder mode during concurrent folder creation
questions: When a concurrent call finds a folder after another call has created it but before that call has set its required mode, must the finder set or verify the mode before using the folder, wait for the creator, or accept it immediately?

quotes:
a folder it finds is accepted, whoever created it, also a concurrent call, when it is a
   folder, and a creation that finds the folder already there is not a failure; a missing one is created with the mode of the imported `STORE_FOLDER_MODE` constant in the
   binary store and of the imported `STATE_FOLDER_MODE` constant in the state folder, set whatever the
   process umask.
judgement.why: The race behavior and mode check performed by a folder-creation operation are operation-level semantics owned by State 5.

topics.topic: Whether project lock files use direct final-path creation or temporary-file-and-rename
questions: Is the project lock file an exception that must be opened or atomically created directly at its final address, or must it also use the temporary-file-and-rename protocol stated for each file?

quotes:
Each file is written to a temporary name in its folder, synchronised to disk and renamed, and
   its folder is synchronised, so a reader sees a complete file or none.

The lock file is created on
   first use with the mode of the imported `LOCK_FILE_MODE` constant and never removed; it holds no content. It is opened for reading and writing,
   created when absent, without following a link, and given the mode of `LOCK_FILE_MODE` each time it is
   opened, whatever the umask; a failure to set that mode is refused like a lock file that cannot be
   opened.
judgement.divergence: One implementation creates every file through a temporary inode and rename, while another opens or creates the lock directly at its final address; concurrent delivery callers observe whether one shared lock serializes both calls.
judgement.why: The universal temporary-file rule includes lock files, while the lock rule requires opening and creating the lock at its address.

topics.topic: Whether the no-removal rule permits internal temporary-file cleanup
questions: Must this prohibition exclude internal temporary-file cleanup, or must the changed A6 rule that removes a temporary file before rename be changed?

quotes: removal of anything, which the first version does not offer (A3).

A write
   that fails before the rename leaves the destination as it was, whether absent or holding an earlier
   complete file, and removes its temporary file; when that removal fails too, the write's own failure is the
   result and the temporary file stays, as after a crash.
judgement.divergence: One implementation removes the temporary file after a failed pre-rename write, while another leaves it because delivery_store is forbidden to own any removal; the destination-folder operator notices the leftover entry.
judgement.why: The module prohibition literally excludes all removal, while A6 explicitly assigns temporary-file removal during failed-write cleanup.
